name: Chemistry
description: Matter, atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, redox, electrolysis, reaction kinetics and organic chemistry for the Nigerian senior secondary curriculum, aligned to WAEC, NECO and JAMB.

topics.name: Particulate Nature of Matter
topics.summary: Matter is made of particles in constant motion; how their arrangement explains states, changes and separation.

subtopics.name: Particles and the States of Matter
subtopics.summary: Kinetic theory, the three states of matter and the changes of state between them.

objectives.text: State the main assumptions of the kinetic theory of matter
Compare the arrangement, motion and energy of particles in solids, liquids and gases
Name and describe the changes of state, including sublimation

subtopics.name: Physical and Chemical Changes
subtopics.summary: Telling a physical change from a chemical change, and classifying matter as element, compound or mixture.

objectives.text: Distinguish physical changes from chemical changes using clear criteria
Classify a sample of matter as an element, a compound or a mixture
Compare the properties of a mixture with those of a compound

subtopics.name: Separation Techniques
subtopics.summary: Choosing filtration, distillation, chromatography or crystallisation to separate a given mixture.

objectives.text: Describe the common laboratory methods used to separate mixtures
Select the appropriate separation method for a stated mixture
Explain the physical property each separation method depends on

topics.name: Atomic Structure and Periodicity
topics.summary: The subatomic particles, how electrons are arranged and how that arrangement drives the periodic table.

subtopics.name: Subatomic Particles and Isotopes
subtopics.summary: Protons, neutrons and electrons, atomic and mass number, and calculating relative atomic mass from isotopes.

objectives.text: State the relative mass, charge and location of each subatomic particle
Use atomic number and mass number to work out particle counts in atoms and ions
Calculate relative atomic mass from isotopic abundances

subtopics.name: Electron Configuration
subtopics.summary: Filling shells and subshells with the Aufbau principle, and linking configuration to position in the periodic table.

objectives.text: Write the electron configuration of atoms of the first twenty elements
Apply the Aufbau principle, Hund rule and Pauli exclusion principle
Deduce group and period from an electron configuration

subtopics.name: Periodic Trends
subtopics.summary: How atomic radius, ionisation energy, electronegativity and metallic character vary across periods and down groups.

objectives.text: Describe the trend in atomic radius across a period and down a group
Explain trends in ionisation energy and electronegativity using nuclear charge and shielding
Predict the metallic or non-metallic character of an element from its position

topics.name: Chemical Bonding
topics.summary: Why atoms combine, the main types of bond, and how bonding controls the properties of a substance.

subtopics.name: Ionic and Covalent Bonding
subtopics.summary: Electron transfer versus electron sharing, and the properties each type of bonding produces.

objectives.text: Explain ionic bonding as the transfer of electrons between atoms
Explain covalent bonding as the sharing of electron pairs
Relate melting point, conductivity and solubility to the type of bonding present

subtopics.name: Metallic Bonding and Intermolecular Forces
subtopics.summary: The sea of delocalised electrons in metals, plus hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces between molecules.

objectives.text: Describe metallic bonding and use it to explain metallic properties
Distinguish intermolecular forces from covalent bonds within a molecule
Use hydrogen bonding to explain the anomalous properties of water

topics.name: Stoichiometry and the Mole Concept
topics.summary: Counting particles by weighing: moles, formulae, reacting masses and the concentration of solutions.

subtopics.name: The Mole Concept
subtopics.summary: The mole, Avogadro constant and molar mass, and converting between mass, moles and number of particles.

objectives.text: Define the mole and state the value of the Avogadro constant
Convert between mass, number of moles and molar mass
Calculate the number of particles in a given amount of substance

subtopics.name: Empirical and Molecular Formulae
subtopics.summary: Working out the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms from masses or percentages, then scaling to the molecular formula.

objectives.text: Calculate an empirical formula from masses or percentage composition
Deduce a molecular formula from an empirical formula and relative molecular mass
Calculate the percentage by mass of an element in a compound

subtopics.name: Reacting Masses and Volumes
subtopics.summary: Using a balanced equation and the mole ratio to predict how much product a given mass of reactant gives.

objectives.text: Balance a chemical equation and read the mole ratio from it
Calculate the mass of product formed from a given mass of reactant
Identify the limiting reactant and calculate percentage yield

subtopics.name: Concentration of Solutions
subtopics.summary: Expressing concentration in mol/dm3 and g/dm3, and preparing or diluting a standard solution.

objectives.text: Calculate concentration in mol per cubic decimetre and in grams per cubic decimetre
Convert between the two concentration units using molar mass
Apply the dilution relationship to prepare a solution of required concentration

topics.name: States of Matter and Gas Laws
topics.summary: How pressure, volume and temperature of a gas are related, and how to use molar volume in calculations.

subtopics.name: Boyle's, Charles' and the General Gas Law
subtopics.summary: Pressure-volume and volume-temperature relationships combined into the general gas equation.

objectives.text: State Boyle's law and Charles' law and give their mathematical forms
Apply the general gas equation to find an unknown pressure, volume or temperature
Convert temperatures to kelvin before using any gas law

subtopics.name: Molar Volume and Gas Calculations
subtopics.summary: Avogadro's law, the 22.4 dm3 molar volume at s.t.p. and gas volume calculations from equations.

objectives.text: State Avogadro's law and the molar volume of a gas at s.t.p.
Convert between the volume of a gas at s.t.p. and the number of moles
Calculate reacting gas volumes using Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes

topics.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
topics.summary: Definitions of acids and bases, the pH scale, salt preparation and quantitative titration work.

subtopics.name: Properties of Acids and Bases
subtopics.summary: Arrhenius and Bronsted-Lowry definitions, basicity, strength and the typical reactions of acids and bases.

objectives.text: Define acids and bases using the Arrhenius and Bronsted-Lowry models
Distinguish between a strong acid and a concentrated acid
Write equations for the characteristic reactions of acids

subtopics.name: pH and Indicators
subtopics.summary: The pH scale, calculating pH from hydrogen ion concentration and choosing the right indicator.

objectives.text: Relate pH to hydrogen ion concentration and calculate simple pH values
State the colour changes of common acid-base indicators
Select a suitable indicator for a given titration

subtopics.name: Salts and Their Preparation
subtopics.summary: Normal, acid and basic salts, solubility rules and the four main routes to preparing a salt.

objectives.text: Classify salts as normal, acid, basic or double salts
Apply solubility rules to predict whether a salt dissolves in water
Choose and describe a suitable preparation method for a named salt

subtopics.name: Volumetric Analysis
subtopics.summary: Titration technique and the calculations that turn a titre value into an unknown concentration.

objectives.text: Describe the correct procedure for carrying out an acid-base titration
Use the titration relationship to calculate an unknown concentration
Calculate an average titre from concordant burette readings

topics.name: Redox Reactions
topics.summary: Oxidation and reduction as electron transfer, oxidation numbers, and balancing redox equations.

subtopics.name: Oxidation and Reduction
subtopics.summary: The oxygen, hydrogen and electron definitions of redox, plus oxidising and reducing agents.

objectives.text: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen, hydrogen and electrons
Identify the oxidising agent and the reducing agent in a reaction
Recognise common laboratory oxidising and reducing agents and their tests

subtopics.name: Oxidation Numbers and Balancing Redox Equations
subtopics.summary: Assigning oxidation numbers with the standard rules and using them to balance half equations.

objectives.text: Apply the rules for assigning oxidation numbers in compounds and ions
Use changes in oxidation number to identify what is oxidised and reduced
Balance a redox equation using the half equation method

topics.name: Electrolysis
topics.summary: Conduction in electrolytes, what happens at each electrode, and the quantitative laws of electrolysis.

subtopics.name: Electrolytes and Electrode Processes
subtopics.summary: Electrolytes and non-electrolytes, preferential discharge, and the products at anode and cathode.

objectives.text: Distinguish electrolytes from non-electrolytes and explain electrolytic conduction
Write the half equations occurring at the anode and the cathode
Apply the factors governing preferential discharge of ions

subtopics.name: Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis
subtopics.summary: Linking charge passed to mass deposited, using the faraday and the quantity of electricity.

objectives.text: State Faraday's first and second laws of electrolysis
Calculate the quantity of electricity from current and time
Calculate the mass or volume of a substance liberated at an electrode

topics.name: Rates of Reaction and Equilibrium
topics.summary: What controls how fast a reaction goes, and how reversible reactions settle into a dynamic equilibrium.

subtopics.name: Rate of Reaction
subtopics.summary: Collision theory and the effect of concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts on rate.

objectives.text: Explain reaction rate using collision theory and activation energy
Describe how each factor changes the rate of a reaction and why
Interpret a graph of product formed against time

subtopics.name: Chemical Equilibrium
subtopics.summary: Reversible reactions, the features of dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier's principle in industry.

objectives.text: Describe the characteristics of a dynamic equilibrium
Apply Le Chatelier's principle to predict the effect of a change
Write an equilibrium constant expression for a given reaction

topics.name: Organic Chemistry
topics.summary: Hydrocarbons and oxygen-containing families: naming, structure, reactions and everyday uses.

subtopics.name: Alkanes
subtopics.summary: The saturated hydrocarbon series, IUPAC naming, isomerism and substitution reactions.

objectives.text: State the general formula of alkanes and name the first ten members
Draw and name the structural isomers of a given alkane
Write equations for the combustion and substitution reactions of alkanes

subtopics.name: Alkenes and Alkynes
subtopics.summary: Unsaturated hydrocarbons, the addition reactions that identify them, and polymerisation.

objectives.text: State the general formulae of alkenes and alkynes and name their members
Describe the addition reactions of unsaturated hydrocarbons
Explain the test that distinguishes an alkene from an alkane

subtopics.name: Alkanols and Alkanoic Acids
subtopics.summary: Alcohols and carboxylic acids: functional groups, fermentation, oxidation and esterification.

objectives.text: Identify the hydroxyl and carboxyl functional groups and name simple members
Describe the preparation of ethanol by fermentation
Write equations for oxidation of alkanols and for esterification

topics.name: Metals and Non-metals
topics.summary: The activity series, extraction and corrosion of metals, and the chemistry of important non-metals.

subtopics.name: Reactivity Series and Extraction of Metals
subtopics.summary: Ordering metals by reactivity, using displacement, and choosing an extraction method to match.

objectives.text: Recall the order of the common metals in the activity series
Predict whether a displacement reaction will occur
Relate the method of extraction of a metal to its position in the series

subtopics.name: Non-metals and Their Compounds
subtopics.summary: Preparation, properties and tests for the common laboratory gases and non-metal compounds.

objectives.text: Describe the laboratory preparation of common non-metal gases
State the confirmatory test for each common laboratory gas
Explain the industrial and environmental importance of key non-metal compounds
